explain.say: Do you love stories? Every good one is like a journey with three parts: a beginning, a middle and an end. Look at the board. Meet Kwame. At the beginning, he is flying his new kite in the park. The beginning tells us who and where.

faq.q: What happens at the beginning of a story?
faq.a: The beginning tells you who the story is about, where it happens and when. Kwame flying his kite in the park is a beginning.
asks: How do I start a story?

faq.q: What happens in the middle of a story?
faq.a: In the middle a problem happens and the character tries to fix it. That is the exciting part that keeps you reading.
asks: What is the problem in a story?

faq.a: The ending solves the problem and shows how the character feels now. It can also show what they learned.
asks: How do I end a story?

faq.q: How do I plan a story?
faq.a: Draw three boxes. In the first, draw who and where. In the second, draw the problem. In the third, draw how it is solved. Then write a few sentences for each box.

faq.q: Why do stories need a problem?
faq.a: Without a problem nothing much happens, and the reader gets bored. The problem makes us wonder what will happen next.
asks: Does every story need a problem?

facts: Anansi the spider stories from West Africa often follow beginning, problem and clever ending.
Many stories around the world follow the same pattern: a character, a problem, and a solution.
